correctness.rationale: The stationary flows have fixed pair sums ell_i opposite state i and a common oriented current j by conservation, exhausting the feasible matrices for |j|<=J. The two directed-triangle determinant terms give det P=(ell_1 ell_2 ell_3+j^2)/(4u); trace zero and the stationary root give residual discriminant (g-j^2)/u. Reversibility at j=0 makes g>=0, and g=0 forces uniform pi by the diagonal of the two-eigenvalue spectral decomposition. For pi=(p,q,r), ell_2 ell_3=-J+4qr, hence J^2-g=(4-9p)qr. The radius is strictly decreasing in j^2 up to g and increasing beyond it, so the exact optimizer has j^2=min(g,J^2). This gives the claimed 4/9 frontier, both branches, all sign choices and the uniform merger. The oriented triangle in the sign direction of j is positive, and some two-cycle is positive at every optimizer (the only possible loss of all reverse edges is a uniform-law endpoint, not optimal); this gives primitivity. A diagonalizable double root -1/2 would force P=-I/2+3(1 pi)/2 and hence uniform pi, proving the nonuniform Jordan claim. Independent exact examples at p=2/5, 4/9 and 9/20 verify existence of the real/complex split, equality at the frontier, and optimal radii 1/2, 1/2 and 2/3 respectively.
residual_risks: The script's check tally is a reported counter and the sampled optimal-envelope comparison uses floating-point square roots. The symbolic proof and rational spot checks, not the reported tally, justify the result. The boundary p=1/2 is outside scope.

evidence: a90ff98542db gives a three-letter no-repeat kernel P_ij=q_j/(1-q_i) for i distinct from j and the symmetric zero-diagonal fixed-composition stationary flow. This flow equals the j=0 slice: conservation determines its undirected pair sums and a symmetric flow has no circulation.

checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md and exact flow calculation
value.rationale: Prescribing the stationary law and prohibiting self-loops are natural joint constraints for a transition design. The result determines exactly when the trace obstruction is attainable, where complex spectra can occur, and when the spectrally best design is necessarily defective. The latter warns against interpreting optimally small eigenvalue modulus as a uniform finite-time mixing guarantee.
residual_risks: This is a three-state eigenvalue-modulus optimization, not a finite-time, higher-dimensional, or population-dynamics result.
